comparator.name: Bachelor Systems Engineering, Policy Analysis & Management
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 1 November 2026 review: adopted OER Annex3 pp18–20 gives 12+12+5 unique components, 60+60+60=180EC for the 2026 entrant, with nominal later years explicitly 2027–2028/2028–2029. Art6 has no formal specialisations, but a required technology-domain choice before semester2; Energy & Industry is first in the official current list and selected independently of UCR. Only its six domain modules are counted. Embedded skills add no separate EC. Dutch full-time programme; English labels follow current guide where supplied, otherwise faithful translations. OER Annex4 p21 requires >45 first-year EC for later-year participation, subject to approved exception; ordinary completion of the first120EC satisfies both progression and BEP entry (all Y1 plus all but at most5EC Y2). Minor30EC remains genuine approved space. BEP15EC counted once, ordinarily Q3–Q4. Erratum corrects the old-TB111C transition destination to current TB111E and removes its old project/teamwork assessment; no old TB111C/D replacement is counted. Current official course-guide entries corroborate methods and domain content; expected prior knowledge is not an extra formal pass threshold. Later offerings remain subject to the applicable annual arrangements.

core: Problem analysis and governance of socio-technical systems, including actor conflict and policy implementation
Public administration, law, institutions, markets, ethics and qualitative governance research
Mathematics, probability, statistics, programming, simulation and optimisation for analysing decisions

Data, digitalisation and responsible technology governance
Transport, logistics and resilient infrastructure governance

alternatives.label: Energy systems, modelling & public policy
alternatives.labelReason: The final selection sustains energy technology, quantitative methods and public governance.
alternatives.concept: A programme combining energy resources, conversion and renewable-system design with mathematical modelling, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Economics, law, qualitative research, EU policymaking, public-policy analysis and sustainability governance connect technological choices with public decisions and competing interests. Climate science and life-cycle assessment support evaluation of energy transitions. It provides a substantive interdisciplinary response to the Energy & Industry direction, with gaps in industrial-process engineering, agent-based and system-dynamics simulation, specialist infrastructure economics and safety, and Delft’s compulsory final project.
progression: All current formal prerequisites occur earlier and all six fixed counselor terms are covered. Programming and calculus precede their dependants; linear algebra precedes numerical/linear-systems work, probability precedes AI decision methods, economics precedes public economics, and energy foundations precede renewable design. Open-entry law, EU politics and climate study may occur later; no extra prerequisite is invented. PPD is in year one; each programme has at least six advanced courses.

alternatives.label: Data systems, decision methods & public policy
alternatives.labelReason: The final selection sustains computing, data methods and institutional/policy analysis without claiming a prescribed public-sector project.
alternatives.concept: A programme centred on programming, software, databases and digital networks, supported by statistical learning, algorithms, probability, numerical methods and optimisation. Law, economics, public-policy analysis, AI ethics and organisational research address the institutional and social decisions surrounding digital systems. Its priority is computational analysis and the governance of digital change, rather than energy technology. Technical projects are not guaranteed to concern public policy; the programme does not reproduce Delft’s full engineering-and-policy sequence or its compulsory final project.
progression: All current formal prerequisites occur earlier and all six fixed counselor terms are covered. Programming and calculus precede their dependants; linear algebra precedes numerical/linear-systems work, probability precedes AI decision methods, economics precedes public economics, and energy foundations precede renewable design. Open-entry law, EU politics and climate study may occur later; no extra prerequisite is invented. PPD is in year one; each programme has at least six advanced courses.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten different courses per programme (75 EC each). Energy, climate, physical sustainability, qualitative inquiry and EU/sustainability governance give way to software, networks, databases, algorithms, machine/deep learning, AI ethics and organisational analysis. This changes the central technical object and methods, with common economics, law and policy providing continuity; differences are not substitutions made only to clear the numerical floor.

candidates.label: Data systems, decision methods & public policy

trace: Direct: AI innovation, labour, business organisation, governance and regulation connect digital tools with institutional and economic consequences; no technical AI content is inferred.
Direct: microeconomic choice, markets and macroeconomic policy foundations support analysis of incentives and market-government relations.
Direct: public goods, externalities, taxation and efficiency/equity supply policy-economics tools; not a substitute for dedicated infrastructure contracts and regulation.
Direct: research design, sampling, experimentation and inferential statistics underpin empirical analysis of decisions and policy.

Complementary: organisational psychology across people, teams and structures, with a systematic review, supports the organisational side of digital change; not public law or technical systems engineering.
Direct: AI ethics and social consequences examine responsibility, fairness and human values in digital decision systems; not the whole external safety course.
Direct: probabilistic/Bayesian reasoning, Markov decision models, expected utility and multi-agent decisions analyse uncertainty and decision behaviour; no public-policy application is assumed.
Direct: search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation implement quantitative decision tools, with algorithmic experiments.
Direct: network protocols and operating-system resources, scheduling and memory management provide technical digital-infrastructure content.
Direct: relational design, normalisation, SQL and query processing provide the data-management layer of digital systems.
Direct: software design, programming paradigms, testing and version control turn computational methods into implemented digital systems.
Direct: algorithm design, data structures and complexity analysis supply efficient computational methods for the data-systems programme.
Direct: cleaning, manipulating and visualising data and a data-analysis project support empirical system and policy investigation; no policy-specific project is promised.
Direct: regression, classification, dimension reduction, validation and predictor projects develop empirical modelling for data-informed decisions, without guaranteeing policy datasets.
Direct: neural-network methods and time/text/image learning extend predictive analysis; no claim of public-sector application or explanatory policy causality.
Direct: structured programming, functions, testing and debugging implement the computational foundation of model-based analysis.
Direct: calculus, differential equations and a Mathematica dynamic-model project establish mathematical model formulation; linear algebra is taught separately.
Direct: matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues and linear systems provide the mathematical structure used in quantitative system analysis.
Direct: numerical roots, quadrature and differential/linear-system solution with error and stability analysis support computational modelling.

Complementary: continuous/discrete linear dynamics, transforms and feedback give rigorous physical-system modelling for the energy concept. Linear time-invariant analysis is not socio-technical ABM or system dynamics.
Direct: probability, statistical inference, Bayesian ideas and sampling simulation support measurement and decision uncertainty.

Direct: institutions, power, networks, stakeholder matrices and policy evaluation examine collective sustainability decisions; energy/climate cases and policy advice connect governance with technical change.
Direct: integrated physical sustainability, thermochemical/mechanical foundations and simple dynamic models introduce resource and environmental constraints on energy systems.

Complementary: waves, chemical principles, material behaviour and engineering/greenwashing cases strengthen the physical and evaluative basis for renewable design, without supplying process engineering.
Direct: climate-system mechanisms and human influence connect energy transition decisions to their physical environmental consequences.
Direct: environmental, social and cost life-cycle assessment of products, processes and services provides explicit criteria for evaluating transition choices.
Direct: renewable resources, conversion, storage, grids and demand management, quantitative exercises and mini-grid/Polysun activities supply substantial actual energy-system study.

Direct: energy-demand/conservation and solar, wind and bioenergy are examined through technical-economic analysis and a partner report. No thermodynamic-cycle or industrial-process sequence is inferred.

Direct: public/private law, constitutional/administrative principles and legal interpretation support the institutional analysis of public decisions. It is not the complete Dutch public-administration sequence.
Direct: normative theories, moral argument and ethical essays supply critical evaluation of decisions and responsibility; not engineering-safety certification.

Direct: EU institutions, interests, agenda setting, legislation and implementation are studied through empirical amendment coding and process tracing, giving concrete multi-actor policymaking rather than generic governance context.
Direct: public-policy formation, globalisation and a sugar-policy case develop policy analysis and policy memos; energy/digital assignments are not guaranteed.
Direct: qualitative research design, interviews, documents, coding, reflexivity and an actual team inquiry support actor- and institution-focused policy research.
blocks: Research questions, design, sampling, statistical analysis and methodological limits share the empirical research function; the external policy-oriented multivariate project is more specific.
Linear programming, discrete optimisation and decision algorithms directly overlap; the external preference-aggregation and complete graph-theory sequence are not reproduced.

Regression, classification and dimension reduction are substantial shared multivariable methods. Prediction-focused statistical learning is not the complete external conjoint/Q-method and survey-measurement curriculum.
Programming foundations, control structures and implementation overlap directly; the prescribed language, applications and credit weight differ.
Dynamic mathematical model formulation and implementation overlap with modelling principles; the wider model taxonomy, stochastic experiments and validation cycle are not reproduced.
Linear algebra is a major explicitly named part of the external module. Differential equations are distributed elsewhere in UCR; this is not a full module equivalence.
Probability and statistical inference are central shared methods; the level, software and balance of applied data analysis differ.
Qualitative case inquiry, interviews, document work and analysis/reporting directly share the principal research method; policy context and project structure differ.
No selected course directly teaches the external complex socio-technical simulation cycle, emergence, queues and agents. Linear Systems is physical LTI analysis and cannot stand in for it.

No separate selected course substantially covers multivariable calculus alongside linear algebra. Single-variable Mathematical Methods and the separately aligned Linear Algebra do not supply that combined module.
No selected course teaches the prescribed agent-based and system-dynamics modelling methods. Generic programming, linear dynamics and machine learning do not establish this relationship.
No selected course guarantees an ABM/system-dynamics socio-technical simulation project; general software or numerical projects are insufficient.
Microeconomic choice and market analysis are central shared foundations; infrastructure-specific economics is less extensive.

Public goods, market failures and government intervention supply a directly relevant economic foundation; specialised infrastructure ownership, contracting and regulatory economics are not equivalent.

Institutions, actor power, governance networks, qualitative stakeholder inquiry and policy evaluation directly address the governing of socio-technical sustainability systems. The case emphasis and prescribed external research design differ.
Public/private law, constitutional-administrative principles and legal reasoning are substantial shared content; Dutch public-administration and EU-law breadth differ.
Normative ethical reasoning is a substantial shared foundation; engineering risk and safety methods remain a gap.

EU institutions, actor interests, decision rules and implementation directly address institutional public decision-making; Dutch administrative-law remedies and the full network-governance sequence differ.

The full actor/objectives/causal/system-diagram and multi-criteria problem-analysis sequence has no separate adequate selected counterpart; later policy and decision courses supply related parts without becoming this introductory integrated module.
Stakeholder reasoning occurs in sustainability governance and policy study, but no separate selected course supplies the dedicated multi-actor-system analysis module.

No separate selected course teaches electricity/gas/heat market structures and governance options at this specialist depth. Sustainability governance is aligned with the broader socio-technical-governance module; energy cases do not become a full energy-market-governance course.
Energy resources, conversion, electricity/storage and demand-system analysis overlap substantially; industrial-network coverage differs.
Technical-economic assessment of energy options is a substantive shared educational function; the external linear-programming and network-performance methods are not reproduced by this course.

Thermal-plant and storage-performance analysis with climate effects has no separate adequate selected counterpart. Renewable design is aligned with advanced performance analysis; the full thermal-plant course remains distinct.
The heat, mass and momentum transfer sequence, transport equations and fluid-flow calculations lack a direct selected counterpart; the title does not refer to logistics.
No selected course supplies the dedicated thermodynamics, exergy, cycle/process simulation and plant-performance sequence.
No selected course supplies industrial unit operations, reactors/separations, flowsheets and mass-balance analysis of industrial clusters.
Genuine 30-EC approved minor remains open; no UCR course is equated with unspecified choices.
Compulsory independent 15-EC bachelor project remains distinct from the scheduled taught courses. The standard optional UCR research element is comparison-only.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic. The current official domain page and OER list Energy & Industry, Data & Digitalisation and Transport & Logistics; none is established as the uniquely broad default. Use their official order as a neutral tie-break. OER Art6 calls these required technology domains, not formal specialisations. The chosen domain is followed throughout; no mixing of mutually exclusive domain modules and no choice based on UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two programmes pass. The core implements substantive energy systems, quantitative analysis and public governance; the data direction changes ten courses and its central technical object. A strongest transport/logistics attempt considered graph/network-flow algorithms (DISCOMP312), GIS/spatial analysis (ENSSUST315), nature-based infrastructure (ENSDELT111), water engineering/governance (ENSDELT211), international business (BENENTR312), decision methods and public economics. Their real content can support algorithms, spatial/environmental or water-governance study, but it does not sustain a transport/logistics organising concept: mobility networks, service/freight operations and transport policy are not taught as a coherent sequence. Water/nature and market-entry studies cannot be relabelled as transport engineering or logistics. The rejected third is an academic feasibility judgment, not an offering failure or title-only judgment. No unrelated substitute is manufactured; the complete candidate attempt and course contributions are in the case evidence.

notes.text: Delft integrates mathematical and computational methods with public administration, law, economics and one technology domain. These UCR programmes combine substantial related study across courses. Shared rows identify partial academic relationships, with deliberate gaps for specialist content.

UCR does not reproduce the industrial-process, heat-and-mass-transfer, agent-based/system-dynamics simulation, specialised infrastructure-economics and engineering-safety sequence. Delft also requires a 15-EC final project. UCR’s optional independent research is shown separately from each scheduled 180-EC programme.

audience.programmeDescription: Delft’s Systems Engineering, Policy Analysis & Management bachelor examines technological systems together with the people, institutions and policies that govern them. It combines engineering analysis, mathematical and computational methods, economics, law and governance. Students choose a technology domain; the curriculum shown follows Energy & Industry.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The energy option combines actual energy-system study with quantitative methods and public policy. The data option shifts the technical emphasis to computing, data analysis and digital systems, retaining law, economics and policy. Both offer substantive related study, with different specialist coverage and project requirements from Delft.

curriculum.limitation: Dutch full-time bachelor. Later years follow the nominal structure for this entrant cohort. The 30-EC minor remains open within approved options.
